title: Temperance

seo.title: Destiny matrix 14 — Temperance: meaning of the arcanum
seo.description: Measure, an even pace and joining things: that is arcanum 14, Temperance. What it means in the destiny matrix, in its strong and weak versions.

meaning: The fourteenth arcanum in the destiny matrix is the energy of measure and of joining. What 14 means: by nature such a person mixes and evens things out — takes two forces that will not meet and finds the right proportion between them. The easiest way to grasp it is the picture on the card, where an angel pours liquid from one cup into another without spilling a drop: 14 makes nothing new out of emptiness and tears nothing old down to the ground, it brings what already exists into one even flow.

This energy believes that the truth lies in the middle and that extremes do harm. From there come both its main strength and its pace: where others throw themselves from fire into ice, the fourteenth dilutes one with the other and keeps an even current. Such an arcanum plays the long game: a steady stride overtakes the bursts that burn out fast. Its engine is not passion or pressure, but an exact dose and patience.

Living as this arcanum means feeling other people’s tension all the time and reaching out to smooth it. From the inside it works like being a pair of scales: you hold the balance between the sides, and the better you hold it, the less anyone notices what it costs. Here the main conflict hides: forever levelling out what is around them, a person stops hearing their own tilt — their own wish, which is exactly the “extreme” they are used to diluting.

A strong fourteen is the master of proportion: it brings people and processes together, carries long things through to a result and still stays itself. The weak version is when measure degrades into half-measures: afraid of tipping the cup, a person never goes all the way with anything and ends up with lukewarm water instead of a living taste. The difference between the versions is not in the power of the number, but in the willingness to choose something whole at least once instead of blending it down to a safe middle.

From its neighbours in the deck the fourteenth differs by refusing sharpness. The thirteenth, Death, cuts off and resets to zero — 14 tears nothing, it moves one state into another smoothly. The fifteenth, The Devil, lives on passion and excess and takes at once — Temperance dilutes that excess on purpose and waits for the right proportion. Where others act by force or by a sudden push, the fourteenth wins by patience and an exact measure.

article.title: Arcanum 14 in the destiny matrix: Temperance and the art of measure
article.short: 14 in the destiny matrix is the Temperance arcanum. It is the energy of the right proportion: the skill of joining two different principles so that neither is lost, keeping a pace you can sustain for years, and letting what matters ripen. Temperance here is not “a little of everything”, and not softness either, but what makes the hard durable and the different compatible. In the plus, 14 brings a sense of measure, taste and a rare knack for reconciling the irreconcilable. In the minus, it brings the lukewarm water of endless compromise, or a seesaw from one extreme to the other.

seo.title: Destiny matrix 14: meaning of the Temperance arcanum
seo.description: Destiny matrix 14 is Temperance, the arcanum of right proportion: character, talent, money and love, where 14 sits in a chart and where it never can.

sections.h2: What 14 means in the destiny matrix
paragraphs: If you had to sum up the arcanum in one sentence: 14 knows how much of each thing is needed. Not equal shares, but the right proportion. A pinch of salt in a pot of soup is measure; half salt, half soup is not. A person with a strong 14 senses such proportions almost physically: how much to talk and how much to listen, how much to work and how much to rest, how much of your own to give up so that something shared can come of it — and where giving way is no longer an option.
The arcanum holds three skills, and they depend on one another:

ul: **Mixing.** Joining different things — people, tastes, habits, skills — so that a third thing appears that neither side had on its own.
**Measuring.** Finding a proportion and a pace that can be held for a long time: not a sprint and not a standstill, but an even stride.
**Waiting.** Understanding that some things have their own time to ripen, and not poking the dough while it rises.

paragraphs: Arthur Edward Waite, the author of the best-known tarot deck, wrote that the rule of this card “tempers, combines and harmonises the psychic and material natures” of a person — the inner and the outer. Benebell Wen, the author of Holistic Tarot, draws a precise line between it and its neighbour: Justice stands for external balance, while Temperance “is about internal balance”, when two contrasting elements fuse into one.

The arcanum is common: 14 stands somewhere in the matrix report of 68.9% of people, about two in three. For comparison, the rarest arcana appear in the charts of 13% of people, the most frequent in 85%. But at different points 14 does different things, and that is what follows.

sections.h2: Measure is proportion, not the middle
paragraphs: “Temperance” sounds modest, almost dull: a temperate climate, a moderate appetite, moderate views. The Latin word the card’s name comes from is far richer. Temperare means “to mix in the right proportion”. A whole family of words grows from the same root, and each one explains the arcanum better than any definition.

ul: **Temperature** originally meant “due mixture” — the ratio of warm to cold.
**Temperament** in ancient theory was the blend of a person’s four “humours”. Character was understood as a proportion, not as a list of traits.
**Tempera** is paint in which the pigment is mixed with egg yolk. For centuries it was used to paint icons and pictures on wooden panels.

**Tempered tuning** is a way of tuning in which every interval departs ever so slightly from the “pure” one, but no key sounds out of tune. In 1722 Bach wrote The Well-Tempered Clavier — preludes and fugues in all 24 keys — to show that it could be done. A piano tuner, in effect, still tempers today.

**Tempering** is also what metalworkers call the step after hardening. Freshly hardened steel is hard but brittle — a blow can crack it. It is heated again, moderately, and it keeps its hardness but stops breaking.

paragraphs: The last example is the key to 14. Temperance does not cancel strength; it makes strength durable: the hard without measure cracks, the soft without measure spreads. Bronze is harder than both the copper and the tin it is made from: a blend in the right proportion gives a quality that none of its parts had.

In English, temperance also means abstinence from drink — the temperance societies of the nineteenth century took their name from it. But the card is some four hundred years older than that meaning and speaks not of prohibition but of mixing. In the old list of virtues, temperance meant not giving up wine but knowing how to dilute it: the Greeks considered drinking undiluted wine a habit of barbarians.

paragraphs.h3: A card of time and of art

paragraphs: 14 has other names, too. The Russian philosopher Pyotr Ouspensky, in his book Simvoly Taro (The Symbolism of the Tarot, 1912), called this card “Time”. Wen notes that “in notable twentieth-century texts” it is called the Time card. Aleister Crowley renamed it “Art” in his Thoth deck — and that, too, is about proportion: every craft begins with knowing how much of each thing to put in and how long to wait.
Hence the three words the arcanum rests on: blend, measure, time.

sections.h2: What 14 looks like in real life
paragraphs: **The dinner table.** People who would never cross paths in ordinary life end up around one table: relatives, colleagues, an old friend with his own views on everything. An hour later they are talking. Nobody noticed that this was the work of the person with 14: they dropped in a topic at the right moment, moved two people round, defused an argument with a joke before it flared up.

**The argument.** Two people pull in different directions: “let’s go to the sea” and “let’s go to the mountains”. 14 doesn’t work out who is right and doesn’t cut the holiday in half. It looks for a third option — a place that has both, or an order in which each gets what they want. A compromise is a concession. A blend is something new.
**The kitchen.** Someone cooks without a recipe, by eye, and it comes out delicious. That is not luck but a sense of proportion trained over years.

**The long haul.** A team has people who burn bright for a week and then go out, and someone who keeps the same stride all year. After a year, the second has done more. 14 is the arcanum of the marathon, not the sprint.

**After the storm.** People come to the person with 14 when things are bad: after a row, a redundancy, a break-up. They don’t hand out verdicts and don’t rush in to rescue — they bring the temperature back to normal. Wen writes about this card in almost the same words: it comes to “cool what was too hot, heat up what was too cold”, to “restore what was lost” and to “right what is wrong”.
All these scenes share one thing: 14 neither wins nor gives in — it joins.

Gender plays no part in calculating the matrix: a man and a woman born on the same day have the same numbers, and 14 means the same for both. The only difference is where a person is used to applying their sense of measure — in the family, at work, in arguments. The idea that 14 is a “feminine”, soft energy is a misunderstanding. Measure is needed by anyone who wants their strength not to break, and a calm man who doesn’t raise his voice and knows how to reach an agreement is none the weaker for it.

paragraphs: **Lukewarm water.** The most common one. A person blends so well that they themselves disappear from the blend. They give way in advance, before anyone has even asked, and then quietly resent that nobody took their wishes into account. On the outside there is peace and quiet; on the inside, a tally nobody has seen. A measure that leaves out one of the sides is no longer measure but dissolution.

**The seesaw.** Instead of proportion, an alternation of extremes: a month of strict routine, then a week of “oh, to hell with it all”. Each extreme looks like a correction of the last. This is hardening without tempering: a rule that is too rigid cracks, and the person is thrown to the opposite side. Matrix readings also file addictions here, and the logic is clear: an addiction is a measure that a person has handed over to something outside themselves.

**Haste.** 14 is the arcanum of time, and its shadow is impatience. Pushing a relationship that needs a year. Reworking a project that hasn’t had time to start working. Demanding a result of yourself in a week where a season is needed. Or the mirror image: “it’s not the right time yet” stretches out for years.

**The apothecary’s scales.** The search for the perfect proportion turns into perfectionism. Everything must be weighed to the gram, and nothing begins because the proportion isn’t perfect yet. A measure that paralyses is just another loss of measure.

paragraphs.h3: How to tell which way your 14 is working

ul: You can say what you want yourself before you offer a compromise.
Your working rhythm looks like a steady line, not a cardiogram.
After you make peace, the argument really is closed, not just postponed.
You can stop in the middle of a pleasure without bans and without guilt.
You notice when a matter needs waiting out and when it needs a push.

paragraphs: If most of these describe you, your 14 is working in the plus. If you recognised yourself in the traps, that is not a verdict but a pointer to where your measure has slipped.

sections.h2: Where 14 stands in the destiny matrix
paragraphs: The number at each point of the matrix comes from adding other numbers, and sums above 22 are reduced. Because of this, 14 lands at some points often, at others rarely, and at three never. The shares in the table are calculated over all birth dates from 1900 to 2026.

paragraphs: The calling card, point A, is calculated from the day of birth, and 14 stands there for everyone born on the 14th of any month. The calling card is the first minutes of an acquaintance, the layer of a person that others read fastest. With 14 in the calling card, a person enters a conversation without pressure, adjusts to the other person’s pace and lowers the temperature in the room. People say of them: “you feel calm with them”, “doesn’t fuss”, “a grown-up”. The flip side is a first impression that is too even: people don’t understand them straight away, and their politeness is sometimes mistaken for agreement. The same arcanum also leads the first decade of life: the age scale starts from the calling card, so for those born on the 14th the number 14 stands over the stretch from 0 to 10.

The family points are among the most frequent places for 14: the section on support and gifts of the family line comes up with this arcanum for 13.5% of people. In the spiritual lines, the father’s F and the mother’s G, 14 is a family value of measure: the family respected those who could reach agreement, never pushed things to extremes and kept the home in balance. In the material lines, H and I, it is a practice: thrift without stinginess, a reserve for hard times, an even household. The minus of a family 14 is the same as that of the arcanum in general: the rule “anything to avoid a quarrel”, handed down along with the peace.

In purpose, 14 is read by level. Personal: to learn your own measure — not to adjust to someone else’s middle, but to know your own proportion of work and rest, closeness and solitude. Social: to be the one who connects others — a translator between people, departments, generations. Planetary: what will outlive the person — a craft, a school, a tradition that needs years to ripen.

paragraphs.h3: The energy map: where 14 turns up most

paragraphs: The most frequent place for 14 is the chakra table: 44.2% of people have the arcanum there. Most often it stands in the emotions column of [manipura](/encyclopedia/chakra/manipura), and the reason is arithmetic. In the manipura row, physics and energy are the same number — the centre of the chart — and emotions are their sum. So everyone with 7 in the centre gets manipura 7-7-14: two Chariots added together make Temperance. That happens to roughly one person in nine. How speed and measure work in one chart is covered in the reading [The Chariot and Temperance](/encyclopedia/combination/7-14). How to read the whole table is explained in the section [on the energy map](/encyclopedia/position/chakras).

In the reading by decades, 14 appears for 23% of people. The age scale goes round the eight outer points of the chart, ten years for each, and 14 can stand over any decade except the third: the stretch from 20 to 30 is led by the month of birth, and there are only twelve months. The stretch from 40 to 50 is led by the year of birth, so 14 is possible there only for those same people born between 1904 and 1940. A decade under 14 is a time not of dashes but of assembly: bringing back together what drifted apart, finding a rhythm that will last the years ahead. Don’t confuse it with the personal year: the year under arcanum 14 has [a reading of its own](/year/14).

paragraphs.h3: The karmic task and the tails

paragraphs: In the karmic task, point D, 14 stands for 1% of people, and all of them share the same combination: the karmic tail [6-20-14](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/6-20-14) and The Wheel of Fortune in the centre. This is not coincidence but arithmetic: when D equals 14, the other points of the tail are fixed. This tail is about love expressed through giving that silently waits for something back, and the 14 at its root teaches you to hold “giving” and “receiving” in the same hands. The second tail with this arcanum is [6-14-8](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/6-14-8), the rarest of all 26: here 14 stands in the middle. There are no other tails with 14, and it is never the first number of a tail. In all, 14 appears in the karmic tail of 1.2% of people.
Three positions are closed to 14 whatever the date of birth:

ul: **Spiritual task, point B.** It equals the month of birth, and there are twelve months.
**Entry of relationships and the tail, point M.** So 14 never opens either the relationship line or the karmic tail.
**Spiritual purpose.** The sum it is built from never gives 14, whatever the date.

paragraphs: If you were shown 14 at one of these points, either the calculation followed a different scheme, or it is a couple’s matrix, where the points are added up from two charts.

sections.h2: The talent of 14 and the careers that suit it
paragraphs: Talent in the matrix is read along a line of three points: the month of birth, the middle point of talent and the inner point K. 14 never falls on the month, but at the other two points it is frequent: the section “Profession and work you love” comes up with this arcanum for 11.3% of people.

The talent of 14 is a sense of proportion applied to work. Such a person sees how to join what others consider incompatible: two stubborn specialists, an old technology and a new task, a budget and a client’s dream. Wen reads this card in work questions in an unexpected way: “it isn’t that new skills need to be learned” — the skills you already have can be fused with a task they don’t seem meant for. For 14 in talent this is a good hint: your strong move is not yet another course but a new combination of what you can already do.
This gift becomes a profession wherever the result depends on proportion and time:

ul: **The craft of blending:** cooking, confectionery, baking, cheesemaking, perfumery, colour work, ceramics, glass — anywhere it matters how much of each thing goes in and how long to wait.
**Sound and colour:** sound engineer (the stage where the tracks are blended is called, fittingly, mixing), arranger, instrument tuner, restorer.
**People between sides:** translator, mediator, negotiator, HR specialist, project manager who brings departments together.
**Accompanying others:** teacher, mentor, counselling psychologist — work where another person’s pace matters, not only your own.
**The living and the slow:** gardening, landscape design, anything that grows in seasons rather than sprints.

paragraphs: Where the talent of 14 stalls: in work done in spurts. Constant crunches and “I needed it yesterday” rob this arcanum of its main advantage — an even stride. The second trap is the role of the eternal go-between, who gets other people’s conflicts but none of their own results. If you have spent years reconciling everyone but never done your own thing, the talent is working for others.

The money line in the matrix is three points: the entry L, the middle point R2 (people call it “under the dollar”, after the sign on other schools’ charts; on ours it is labelled “Middle of the money line”) and the crossing with the relationship line, R. 14 can stand at any of them, and the section “Money in the destiny matrix” comes up with this arcanum for 11.4% of people.

A curious coincidence: when Waite listed this card’s divinatory meanings, he began with “Economy, moderation, frugality, management”. It is a rare case of an old list of meanings being directly about money — and it fits the matrix well.

**At the entry, point L,** 14 shows which action money begins with: joining. Income comes when a person brings sides together — client and contractor, product and buyer, two partners who would never have agreed on their own — or makes something where proportion decides everything.

**Under the dollar, at point R2,** 14 sets the condition for a stable income: an even pace. Money grows for whoever puts aside a little regularly, keeps spending in proportion to income and doesn’t chase quick money. Sharp moves — a loan for a hot idea, everything on one bet — work badly at this point.

**At the crossing, point R,** money and closeness affect each other. Here 14 wants a budget mixed honestly: not “everything shared” and not “each for themselves”, but an agreed proportion that both understand.

The minus of 14 in money shows in the same seesaw: a month of strict saving — and one day that eats everything saved. Or in dissolving: for years a person doesn’t raise their price because it feels “awkward”, and charges an average rate for above-average work.

What helps: a fixed share of income that is put aside at once rather than “whatever is left”; one spending rule instead of ten bans; a day’s pause before any big purchase. 14 decides best when the decision has been given time to steep.

In the relationships section, 14 appears for 10.2% of people. The entry of the relationship line, point M, is closed to this arcanum, so 14 turns up further along: in the middle of the line, “Under the heart”, at the crossing with money, or at the inner point of talent K, which also feeds into this section. 14 under the heart has [a reading of its own](/encyclopedia/position/love_middle/14).

In love, 14 is pace and blending. A person with this arcanum doesn’t fall in love at a run and doesn’t break things off in one evening. They get close gradually and build what you could call a third thing: a shared household, a shared sense of humour, shared habits in which the two are mixed. It is calm beside them: rows don’t escalate, sharp corners get smoothed, and after a conflict the conversation returns to the matter at hand rather than to old grudges.

The weak spot is the same as in character: the wish for peace is stronger than the wish to be heard. 14 gives way before being asked, adapts to the partner’s schedule and tastes, says “I don’t mind, you choose”. For years this looks like perfect harmony, and then it turns out that one of them has been giving way all along while the other never even knew. A measure that contains only the partner is no measure.
What helps: name your own wish before looking for a compromise, not after; argue about the matter rather than smoothing it over; remember that in a good blend both parts can still be tasted.

Compatibility in the destiny matrix is a separate calculation. Under the common scheme, the matching points of two personal charts are added, the sums are reduced, and the resulting third matrix is read as a chart of the couple itself. Its points mean something different from those in a personal chart: the centre, for example, describes the overall atmosphere between the partners rather than the character of either one. Below is 14 in a couple’s matrix according to Yuliana Lisovskaya’s book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (The Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024). This is her school and her practice, not a general canon.

**In the plus,** 14 makes a couple who argue with words rather than slammed doors: contradictions are settled by talking and compromise, and each understands the other’s needs. There is a balance between activity and quiet time together, and peace of mind is valued above things. Such a couple can be made up of very different people — by background, faith, habits — and the difference doesn’t drive them apart. With money there is no fuss: they spend according to income, don’t compete, and if they borrow, they pay it back.

**In the minus** — an imbalance visible from outside: one keeps giving way, and the other never gives it a thought. There is no common language and no sense of safety, there is a chill between the two; one of them shuts themselves off from family problems. In money, the same imbalance: one saves, the other spends, or one depends on the other.

The task of such a couple, according to Lisovskaya, is to reach agreement, not to rush to conclusions about the partner, not to offload their own fears onto them and not to try to control them. The method gives no compatibility percentages: 14 in a couple’s matrix speaks of what the couple needs to work on, not of whether the two people suit each other. 14 in the centre of a personal chart has [a reading of its own](/encyclopedia/position/center/14).

sections.h2: What helps 14 work in the plus

ol: **Your own first, then the shared.** Before you look for a compromise, name — at least to yourself — what you want. A blend without your part is made not of two ingredients but of one.

**Proportion instead of “equal shares”.** In an argument, ask not “how do we make it equal for everyone” but “how much of what does this need”. Sometimes the right proportion is ninety to ten, and that is more honest than half and half.
**Tempering instead of hardening.** If a rule keeps breaking — you hold on, you slip, you hold on again — it is too rigid. Soften it to something you can keep for a year, not a week.
**Time to steep.** Put off important decisions about money, moving or relationships for at least a day. This is not indecision: 14 thinks better when a thought has had time.

**A permitted extreme.** Keep one area where measure isn’t needed: loud music, spicy food, a Sunday of box sets until late at night. An extreme chosen in advance doesn’t build up and doesn’t break through as a seesaw. A measure with no room for an extreme becomes an extreme itself.
**Craft with your hands.** Cooking, mixing paints, mixing sound, pottering in the garden. 14 recovers in work where the proportion is visible and can be tasted.

sections.h2: Temperance in Waite’s deck: what the classic card shows
paragraphs: Next to this section is the card from the deck that Pamela Colman Smith drew in 1909 to Arthur Edward Waite’s design. Almost every symbol usually linked with 14 comes from here.

At the centre stands a winged angel in white. On its forehead is “the sign of the sun”, on its breast “the square and triangle of the septenary”, as Waite calls it: the square is four, the triangle three, together seven. Ouspensky, describing this sign, also placed a point inside the triangle: the triangle is the world of spirit, the square the visible world, the point the human soul. The angel holds two cups, and water flows diagonally between them. One foot stands in the water, the other on the bank. A path leads from the water towards the mountains, and above it is a radiance in which a crown can be made out. Yellow flowers grow by the water — they are usually called irises; Wen calls them lilies.

Waite himself explained the card like this. The angel is pouring “the essences of life from chalice to chalice”, and the one foot on the earth and the other on the waters show the dual nature of these essences. The whole scene, with the path towards the light, is in his words “some part of the Secret of Eternal Life, as it is possible to man in his incarnation”. The familiar readings — “changes in the seasons, perpetual movement of life” — he rejected outright. He thought the card’s name a matter of convention: it is “called Temperance fantastically, because, when the rule of it obtains in our consciousness, it tempers, combines and harmonises the psychic and material natures”. And describing older versions of the card, he remarked that the image “has no especial connexion with Temperance”, seeing in this an instance of “a meaning behind meaning” — the very thing that makes the tarot worth studying at all.

One more detail from Waite’s text: he refers to the angel as “he”, but at once adds that “the figure is neither male nor female”. A good answer to anyone who thinks of 14 as a “feminine” arcanum. The angel is also where 14 gets its “angelic” reputation in popular matrix readings.

The cups have been read in different ways. Ouspensky, who called the card “Time”, saw the past in one cup and the future in the other, and in the stream between them the present, which “flows both ways”; he admitted he could not tell from which cup into which the water was pouring. A hundred years later Wen asks the same question — does the water flow down “with gravity”, or up, “against the laws of physics”? — and sees in the cups the conscious and the unconscious, which the card reconciles.

The formula itself is older than Waite. In medieval art the virtue of Temperance was shown as a woman pouring liquid from one vessel into another — diluting wine with water. The early Italian cards of the fifteenth century kept to the same image.

sections.h2: The Temperance card in a tarot reading
paragraphs: If you came with a question about tarot rather than the matrix, this is how Temperance is read in a spread.

**Upright.** For Waite: “Economy, moderation, frugality, management, accommodation”. For Wen: internal balance and the need to “reconcile two contrasting elements”. In a love question she advises a single person to look at their own behaviour: the difficulties may come from an “internal imbalance”. To a couple, the card speaks of cooperation and of the time to temper “extreme emotions, such as anger, resentment, hostility”. In a career question, it says that new skills are not essential: it is enough to fit what you can already do to the task.

**Reversed.** Waite’s list is unexpected: “Things connected with churches, religions, sects, the priesthood, sometimes even the priest who will marry the Querent; also disunion, unfortunate combinations, competing interests.” Wen reads the reversed card more simply: temperance is needed but not applied — “excess, overflow”, an inability to stop in time.

There are no reversed arcana in the destiny matrix: a number calculated from a date doesn’t lie upside down. The plus and minus of 14 in a chart are not the position of a card but how a person uses their own sense of measure.

sections.h2: Neighbours in the deck and kindred arcana
paragraphs: The meaning of 14 shows clearly through its neighbours. Before it stands Death (13) — an ending after which the old form does not return. After it comes The Devil (15), the arcanum of passion, temptation and attachment. Temperance between them is like the pause between two blows: after an ending, not to throw yourself into the first extreme that comes along, but to make a new blend out of what is left. If 15 is measure lost, 14 is measure held. How these arcana work within one chart is covered in the readings [Death and Temperance](/encyclopedia/combination/13-14) and [Temperance and The Devil](/encyclopedia/combination/14-15).

The second family of 14 is the virtues. Three cards of the deck grew out of the classical list of virtues: Justice, Strength and Temperance. In the Marseilles order the matrix uses, they stand at equal steps — 8, 11, 14. Waite swapped Strength and Justice, but the step stayed the same. The fourth virtue, prudence, is missing from the deck, and where it went is still debated.
All three are about measure, but different kinds of it:

ul: **[Justice (8)](/encyclopedia/arcanum/8)** — measure on the outside: decision, responsibility, an honest account. Wen draws the line in exactly this way: 8 is external balance, 14 internal. Together — in the reading [Justice and Temperance](/encyclopedia/combination/8-14).

**[Strength (11)](/encyclopedia/arcanum/11)** — the measure of force: passion and stubbornness not suppressed but tamed. Together — in the reading [Strength and Temperance](/encyclopedia/combination/11-14).
**Temperance (14)** — the measure of a blend: not one thing defeating the other, but both becoming a third.

paragraphs: And one more comparison from Wen: [The Moon (18)](/encyclopedia/arcanum/18) speaks of the repressed — what a person does not want to see in themselves — while Temperance is about how the repressed and the conscious begin to come to terms.

sections.h2: What this reading is based on

ul: The card’s symbolism and divinatory meanings — A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1910, reissued 1922): the image and its meaning from Part II, the meanings in a spread from Part III.
The modern reading — Benebell Wen, Holistic Tarot (2015), the section on Key 14.
The name “Time” and the reading of the cups — P. D. Ouspensky, Simvoly Taro (The Symbolism of the Tarot, 1912).
The couple’s matrix — Yu. Lisovskaya, Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (The Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024), the chapter on the 14th energy.

Positions and shares — calculated with Natalia Ladini’s classic destiny matrix scheme, running through every birth date from 1 January 1900 to 2026. How the calculation works is explained on the page [about the method](/method).
The readings of positions are our adaptation of the card’s meaning to the role of each point: a way to understand yourself, not a prediction of events.
